body:
Priming means soaking the wick in liquid before you use a new coil or pod. Skipping it is the most common way to ruin one, and it is the cause of many first-puff burnt tastes. The cotton inside a coil is dry when it is new, and if you fire the coil before the cotton is saturated, the dry cotton scorches and the coil never tastes right again. This guide explains why priming matters, how to do it step by step for coils, pods and tanks, how long to wait for different liquids, how to tell that a coil is ready, what to do if you forgot to prime, how to avoid repeat damage and how to choose replacements. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## Why prime
Cotton that is dry burns when heated, leaving a burnt taste that can shorten the coil's life. Soaking ensures the wick is saturated, so that when the coil heats, it vaporizes liquid, not cotton. A new coil that has been primed gives good flavor from the first puff, and a coil that has not been primed may give a harsh taste that never fully goes away. Priming takes only a few minutes and is the single most useful habit for coil life.

## Step by step
1. **Unpack the coil carefully,** and do not touch the cotton or the heating element with your fingers more than necessary.
2. **Drip a few drops of e-liquid directly onto the cotton** through the wicking holes, if the coil has them. Use the same liquid you plan to vape.
3. **Fit the coil into the tank,** and screw it in firmly but not too tightly.
4. **Fill the tank or pod with liquid,** up to the recommended line.
5. **Let it stand for five to ten minutes.** This lets liquid soak into the cotton from all sides.
6. **Take two or three gentle puffs without pressing the fire button, if possible.** This draws liquid through the coil.
7. **Start at a low power, then increase gradually.** Begin at the lower end of the coil's range.

## Pod systems
For refillable pods, fill the pod, let it rest, then draw gently. Do not overfill. For pre-filled pods, let the pod sit for a few minutes after you insert it, especially if it is new, so that the wick soaks from the liquid. Take gentle puffs at first. If the pod is pre-filled and the flavor is harsh from the first puff, give it longer.

## Tanks
For tanks with replaceable coils, prime the coil as above, then fill the tank. Tilt the tank when you fill it, so liquid runs down the side. Check that the airflow is open while you wait, so that liquid can reach the coil. Fill above the wicking holes so that the coil is covered by liquid.

## Thick liquid
Thicker liquids need longer to soak. Wait up to fifteen minutes. High-VG liquids move slowly into cotton, and impatience is the main cause of burnt coils with thick liquid. If you use a very thick liquid, drip a little extra on the cotton, and be gentle at first.

## Signs it is ready
The cotton looks dark and wet, and the first puffs taste like the liquid, not burnt. If you can see the cotton through the wicking holes, it should look fully wet, not pale or dry. The coil should feel as though vapor is smooth, and not give a harsh or acrid taste.

## If you forgot to prime
If you took a puff on a dry coil and it tasted burnt, stop. Let it sit for several minutes with liquid, then try again gently. A mild case may recover, but a truly scorched coil will not. If the burnt taste persists, replace the coil. It is cheaper than puffing through a bad taste. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## Prevent repeat damage
Keep liquid above the minimum and avoid chain vaping. A coil that is kept wet and used gently lasts much longer. Do not run it at higher power than the coil's range. Change liquid flavors thoughtfully, because switching to a very different flavor can leave ghosting, a mix of old and new tastes. See [why vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/) and [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

## Priming different coil types
### Mesh coils
Mesh coils have a large surface of cotton, and they need a good soak. Drip liquid on the cotton and let it rest. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).

### Wire coils
Wire coils with cotton wicks need the same treatment: wet the cotton and wait. Check that the wicking holes are clear.

### Ceramic and other coils
Some coils use ceramic or other materials that absorb liquid slowly. Follow the maker's instructions, and allow extra soaking time.

## A worked example
You buy a new 0.6 ohm mesh coil and a thin fruit liquid. You drip six drops onto the cotton, screw the coil in and fill the tank. You wait ten minutes. You take three gentle puffs without firing, then set 25 watts, in the lower part of the range. The first puffs taste of fruit, not burnt. After a few puffs at 25 watts, you raise to 30 watts, and find it comfortable. The coil lasts for weeks. If you had fired it on a dry wick, it would have burnt in seconds.

## Replace when needed
Check [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). Keep a spare so that you can replace a worn coil right away, and prime it properly each time.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How long should I wait?
Five to ten minutes for most liquids, up to fifteen for thick ones.

### Do I need to prime a pre-filled pod?
Let it sit for a few minutes after you insert it, and start with gentle puffs. The wick usually soaks from the liquid inside.

### Can I prime with a different liquid?
It is best to use the liquid you plan to vape, so that you do not mix flavors.

### What if the coil leaks after priming?
You may have used too much liquid. Wipe the outside, and let it rest upright. See [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

### Does a coil need priming each time I refill?
No. Only a new coil. After that, keep the liquid level up.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The impatient first puff
A customer fitted a new coil and vaped at once. It tasted burnt from the first puff, and the coil was finished within a day. Waiting ten minutes would have saved it. Lesson: patience costs nothing.

### The thick liquid
A customer used a very thick liquid and waited only five minutes. The coil burnt. Waiting fifteen, with extra drops on the cotton, worked well. Lesson: thicker liquid needs longer.

### The pre-filled pod
A pre-filled pod tasted harsh at first. After ten minutes standing, it was smooth. Lesson: even pre-filled pods benefit from a short rest.

## A priming checklist
- Is the coil the right one for the device?
- Are the cotton and wicking holes clean?
- Did you add a few drops to the cotton?
- Did you fill to the recommended line?
- Did you wait at least five to ten minutes?
- Did you start at low power with gentle puffs?

Run through it every time, and your coils will last longer and taste better.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the wait.** It is the most common mistake.
- **Overfilling,** which causes leaks.
- **Starting at high power.** It scorches a new coil.
- **Touching the cotton.** It contaminates it.
- **Switching flavors without rinsing or resting.** It causes ghosting.

## Frequently asked questions about priming
### Is dripping liquid on the cotton necessary?
It helps the cotton soak faster, especially with thick liquid. If the coil design does not expose the cotton, fill the tank and wait instead.

### Can I prime with water?
No. Use the e-liquid you will vape, because water does not belong in a coil.

### What if my pod does not seem to need priming?
Many pre-filled pods are designed to be ready after a short rest. Follow the maker's instructions, and give it a few minutes anyway.

### How do I know I primed enough?
The first puffs taste of the liquid and not of burnt cotton. If they taste harsh, stop and let it rest longer.

## Keeping spares ready
A spare pod or coil, already primed and stored in a clean bag, means that a worn one can be swapped in seconds. Prime a spare when you buy it, so that it is ready when you need it, and store it upright in a cool place. Do not store a primed coil for long periods, because the liquid can settle. Replace the spare when you use it, and note the date so that you rotate stock.

## When priming is not enough
If a coil is faulty from new, no amount of priming will fix it. Signs include a burnt taste from the very first puffs even after a long soak, a device that shows a short-circuit message or a coil that looks damaged. In that case, replace it, and if the coil came from us, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID.
